title: Nouns: Singular & Plural
rule:
SINGULAR = one.  PLURAL = more than one.

RULE 1 — Most nouns: add -s
   cat → cats,  book → books,  bag → bags

RULE 2 — Ends in -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -z: add -es
   bus → buses,  dish → dishes,  box → boxes,  watch → watches

RULE 3 — Consonant + y: y becomes -ies
   baby → babies,  city → cities,  lady → ladies
   (Vowel + y just adds -s: boy → boys, day → days)

RULE 4 — Some -f / -fe: change to -ves
   leaf → leaves,  knife → knives,  wife → wives

RULE 5 — IRREGULAR (memorise these)
   child → children      man → men           woman → women
   foot → feet           tooth → teeth       mouse → mice
   person → people       ox → oxen

RULE 6 — Same in both forms
   sheep, fish, deer, aircraft
ruleZh: 多数名词加 -s。以 s/sh/ch/x 结尾加 -es。辅音+y 改 -ies。有些 f/fe 改 -ves。不规则要背：child→children。有些不变：sheep。

title: Nouns: Countable & Uncountable
rule:
COUNTABLE — you can count them
   one apple, two apples, three cups
   Can be singular or plural.
   Use: a/an, many, few, a few, How many?

UNCOUNTABLE — you cannot count them
   water, rice, sugar, money, advice, information, furniture, homework, bread, milk
   NEVER add -s.  Always treated as singular.
   Use: much, little, a little, some, How much?

TO COUNT UNCOUNTABLE THINGS use a measure word
   a glass of water      a bowl of rice
   a bag of sugar        a piece of advice
   a loaf of bread       a slice of cake

QUICK TEST
   Can you say "two ___"?  Yes = countable.  No = uncountable.

COMMON MISTAKES
   ❌ many rice          ✅ much rice
   ❌ two advices        ✅ two pieces of advice
   ❌ How many money?    ✅ How much money?
   ❌ I bought breads    ✅ I bought bread
ruleZh: 可数名词能数，有复数。不可数名词不能数，永不加 -s。可数用 many，不可数用 much。要数不可数就用量词：一杯水、一碗饭。

opts: I bought three loaves of bread.
I bought a lot of bread.

title: Nouns: Common & Proper
rule:
COMMON nouns — general things.  Small letter.
   city, woman, country, day, river, language

PROPER nouns — specific names.  ALWAYS capital letter.
   Singapore, Mama, Monday, English, Orchard Road

ALWAYS CAPITALISE
   People's names:      Lin, Mr Tan
   Places:              Singapore, Malaysia, Bedok
   Days and months:     Monday, January
   Languages:           English, Chinese, Malay
   Titles:              Doctor Lim, Aunty Lily
   Nationalities:       Singaporean, Chinese

DO NOT capitalise
   Seasons:             summer, winter
   General subjects:    maths, science
   (But languages ARE capitalised: English, Chinese)

COLLECTIVE nouns — a group as one thing
   a family, a team, a class, a group
   Usually take a singular verb: My family IS large.

ABSTRACT nouns — ideas you cannot touch
   love, courage, happiness, freedom, advice
ruleZh: 普通名词是一般事物，小写。专有名词是特定名称，永远大写：人名、地名、星期、月份、语言。季节和一般科目不大写，但语言要大写。

title: Possessives (apostrophe s)
rule:
POSSESSIVE shows who owns something.

SINGULAR owner: add 's
   Mama's bag        the cat's tail        Lin's phone

PLURAL owner ending in -s: add ' only
   the boys' shoes   my parents' house     the girls' school

IRREGULAR PLURAL (no -s): add 's
   the children's toys      the women's group      the men's shirts

NAMES ending in -s: either is accepted
   James's car   or   James' car

THINGS usually use "of" instead
   the leg of the table  (better than 'the table's leg')
   the end of the road

⚠️ ITS vs IT'S — the classic trap
   its  = belonging to it     The dog wagged ITS tail.
   it's = it is               IT'S raining today.
   Possessive pronouns NEVER take an apostrophe:
   yours, hers, ours, theirs, its  (no apostrophe!)
ruleZh: 所有格表示所属。单数加 's（Mama's bag）。复数以 s 结尾只加 '（the boys' shoes）。不规则复数加 's（children's）。注意 its 是所属，it's 是 it is。

title: Pronouns
rule:
A PRONOUN replaces a noun so you don't repeat it.
   Mama cooks. Mama is happy. → Mama cooks. SHE is happy.

SUBJECT — does the action (before the verb)
   I, you, he, she, it, we, they
      SHE cooks.   THEY are playing.

OBJECT — receives the action (after the verb or preposition)
   me, you, him, her, it, us, them
      Help ME.   I saw THEM.   Give it to HER.

POSSESSIVE ADJECTIVE — before a noun
   my, your, his, her, its, our, their
      This is MY bag.

POSSESSIVE PRONOUN — stands alone
   mine, yours, his, hers, its, ours, theirs
      This bag is MINE.

REFLEXIVE — the action returns to the doer
   myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself,
   ourselves, yourselves, themselves
      I cooked it MYSELF.   She hurt HERSELF.

QUICK TEST
   Before the verb → I, he, she
   After the verb → me, him, her
   Before a noun → my, his, her
   Alone → mine, his, hers
ruleZh: 代词代替名词。动词前用 I, he, she；动词后用 me, him, her；名词前用 my, his, her；单独用 mine, hers。反身代词 myself, herself 表示自己。

title: Articles: a, an, the
rule:
A — before a CONSONANT sound
   a cat, a book, a house, a university (yoo sound)

AN — before a VOWEL sound (a e i o u)
   an apple, an egg, an umbrella, an hour (silent h)

⚠️ SOUND matters, not the letter
   a university   (sounds like 'yoo')
   an hour        (h is silent)
   a one-dollar note  (sounds like 'wun')

THE — a specific thing both people know
   THE cat on my sofa.
   Also: the sun, the moon, the world, the market, the sky

NO ARTICLE for
   General plurals:      I like cats.
   General uncountable:  I drink water.
   Names:                Singapore, Mama, English
   Meals:                I eat breakfast.
   Sports:               I play football.
   Going home:           I go home.  (not 'to home')

A vs THE
   I saw A cat.        (first mention, any cat)
   THE cat was black.  (now we both know which)

ALWAYS 'THE' with superlatives
   THE best, THE biggest, THE most important
ruleZh: a 用在辅音音前，an 用在元音音前 —— 看发音不看字母。the 指特定事物。复数泛指、不可数泛指、人名地名、三餐前不加冠词。最高级前一定用 the。

title: Adjectives
rule:
An ADJECTIVE describes a noun.
   a BIG house,  a KIND woman,  DELICIOUS food

WHERE THEY GO
   Before a noun:        a green bag
   After be/look/seem:   The bag IS green.

ORDER when using several
   Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material
      a lovely small old round green Chinese wooden table
   In practice use only two or three.
   ✅ a lovely small red bag    ❌ a red small lovely bag

COMPARING TWO — comparative
   Short words: -er + than       big → bigger than
   Ends in -y: -ier + than       happy → happier than
   Long words: more ... than     more beautiful than
   Irregular: good→better, bad→worse, far→further

COMPARING THREE OR MORE — superlative
   Short: the + -est             the biggest
   Long: the most                the most beautiful
   Irregular: the best, the worst

⚠️ NEVER DOUBLE UP
   ❌ more bigger      ✅ bigger
   ❌ most biggest     ✅ the biggest

AFTER taste / smell / feel / look / sound use an ADJECTIVE not an adverb
   The soup tastes GOOD.  (not 'well')
ruleZh: 形容词描述名词，放名词前或 be 后。比较两个用 -er/more...than；三个以上用 the -est/the most。不能重复：不能说 more bigger。taste/smell/feel 后用形容词。

title: Adverbs
rule:
An ADVERB describes a verb, an adjective, or another adverb.
   She walks SLOWLY.

ADJECTIVE vs ADVERB — the key difference
   Adjective describes a NOUN:  She is a QUICK walker.
   Adverb describes a VERB:     She walks QUICKLY.

MAKING ADVERBS — usually add -ly
   quick → quickly    slow → slowly    careful → carefully
   -y → -ily:         happy → happily
   -le → -ly:         simple → simply

IRREGULAR
   good → WELL   (never 'goodly')
   fast → fast   (no change)
   hard → hard   (no change)
   ⚠️ 'hardly' means ALMOST NOT — completely different!
      I work hard.    = I work with effort
      I hardly work.  = I almost never work

TYPES
   How:        quickly, carefully, well, loudly
   When:       now, later, yesterday, soon, already
   How often:  always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never
   Where:      here, there, outside, everywhere

WHERE FREQUENCY ADVERBS GO
   Before the main verb:  I ALWAYS eat rice.
   After the be verb:     She is ALWAYS happy.

⚠️ After taste, smell, feel, look, sound → use an ADJECTIVE
   ✅ It smells good.   ❌ It smells well.
ruleZh: 副词修饰动词，通常加 -ly。形容词修饰名词。good 的副词是 well。hard 不变，hardly 意思完全不同（几乎不）。频率副词放主动词前、be 动词后。

title: Verb 'to be' (am / is / are)
rule:
'BE' is the most important verb in English.

PRESENT
   I         am     I am tired.
   You       are    You are kind.
   He/She/It is     She is my mother.
   We        are    We are hungry.
   They      are    They are my friends.

PAST
   I         was    I was tired.
   You       were   You were late.
   He/She/It was    He was happy.
   We        were   We were at home.
   They      were   They were busy.

NEGATIVE — add 'not'
   I am not / I'm not
   She is not / She isn't
   They are not / They aren't
   He was not / He wasn't
   We were not / We weren't

QUESTIONS — swap the order
   Are you tired?      Is she your mother?
   Was he happy?       Were they busy?

USE 'BE' FOR
   Feelings:  I am happy.
   Age:       She is forty.
   Jobs:      He is a teacher.
   Weather:   It is hot.
   Location:  We are at home.
ruleZh: be动词最重要。现在时：I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are。过去时：I/he/she/it was, we/you/they were。否定加 not。疑问句把 be 动词放前面。

title: Verb 'to have' (have / has / had)
rule:
'HAVE' has TWO jobs.

JOB 1 — OWNERSHIP (to possess)
   PRESENT
      I / You / We / They  →  HAVE     I have two children.
      He / She / It        →  HAS      She has a green bag.
   PAST — always HAD
      I HAD a cat when I was young.

   Negative:
      I do NOT have money.    /  I don't have money.
      She does NOT have time. /  She doesn't have time.
      I did NOT have money.   (past)
   Questions:
      DO you have children?   DOES she have time?   DID you have lunch?

JOB 2 — HELPER for present perfect
   have / has  +  PAST PARTICIPLE
      I HAVE eaten.       She HAS finished.
      I HAD eaten before you came.  (past perfect)

   Negative: I have NOT eaten.  /  haven't
   Question: HAVE you eaten?

'HAVE GOT' — common in speech, same as 'have'
   I have got two children.  =  I have two children.
   Question: HAVE you got children?

'HAVE TO' — necessity (a rule from outside)
   I HAVE TO work tomorrow.
   She HAS TO see the doctor.
   Past: I HAD TO work yesterday.

⚠️ WATCH OUT
   ❌ She have a bag.        ✅ She has a bag.
   ❌ Does she has time?     ✅ Does she have time?
   ❌ I have ate.            ✅ I have eaten.
ruleZh: have 有两个用法：表示拥有（I have, she has, 过去 had），和作助动词构成完成时（have + 过去分词）。否定用 do/does/did not have。have to 表示必须。注意 does 后面用 have 不是 has。

title: Verb 'to do' (do / does / did)
rule:
'DO' has TWO jobs.

JOB 1 — A REAL ACTION VERB (to perform)
   I DO my homework every day.
   She DOES the washing.
   I DID the cleaning yesterday.

   Forms:  I/You/We/They → DO      He/She/It → DOES      Past → DID

JOB 2 — HELPER for questions and negatives
   (with all verbs EXCEPT 'be' and modals)

   QUESTIONS
      DO you eat rice?          DOES she eat rice?
      DID you eat rice?         (past)
   NEGATIVES
      I DO NOT eat fish.        She DOES NOT eat fish.
      I DID NOT eat fish.       (past)

   ⚠️ THE GOLDEN RULE
   After do / does / did, the main verb stays PLAIN
      ❌ Does she eats?     ✅ Does she eat?
      ❌ Did you went?      ✅ Did you go?
      ❌ She doesn't eats.  ✅ She doesn't eat.

JOB 3 — EMPHASIS (adding strength)
   I DO like it!  (really, truly)
   She DOES try hard.

⚠️ NEVER use do/does/did with 'be' or modals
   ❌ Do you are tired?   ✅ Are you tired?
   ❌ Does she can swim?  ✅ Can she swim?

BOTH JOBS AT ONCE — this looks strange but is correct
   DO you DO your homework?
   She DOESN'T DO the washing.
   DID you DO it?
ruleZh: do 有两个用法：实义动词（做事）和助动词（构成疑问和否定）。I/you/we/they 用 do，he/she/it 用 does，过去用 did。用了 do/does/did 主动词要用原形。be 动词和情态动词不用 do。

title: Present Simple Tense
rule:
PRESENT SIMPLE — habits, routines and facts.
   I eat rice every day.   The sun rises in the east.

FORM
   I / You / We / They  →  plain verb
      I eat.  They walk.
   He / She / It  →  ADD -s
      She eats.  He walks.

THE -s RULE (he/she/it only)
   Most verbs: add -s              walk → walks
   -s, -sh, -ch, -x: add -es       watch → watches
   Consonant + y: y → -ies         study → studies
   Irregular: have→has, go→goes, do→does

NEGATIVE
   I/You/We/They → do not (don't) + plain verb
      I do not eat fish.
   He/She/It → does not (doesn't) + plain verb
      She does not eat fish.   ⚠️ NOT 'does not eats'

QUESTIONS
   Do you eat rice?      Does she eat rice?
   ⚠️ After do/does the verb stays plain.

TIME WORDS often used
   always, usually, often, sometimes, never,
   every day, every week, on Mondays
ruleZh: 现在简单时表示习惯和事实。I/you/we/they 用原形，he/she/it 加 -s。否定用 do not / does not + 原形。疑问用 Do / Does。用了 does 动词不加 -s。

title: Present Continuous (-ing)
rule:
PRESENT CONTINUOUS — happening RIGHT NOW.
   I am cooking.   She is sleeping.   They are playing.

FORM:  am / is / are  +  verb + ing
   I         am  cooking
   He/She/It is  cooking
   We/You/They are cooking

SPELLING OF -ING
   Most verbs: add -ing         walk → walking
   Ends in -e: drop e           make → making,  write → writing
   Short vowel + consonant: double it
                                run → running,  sit → sitting
   Ends in -ie: → -ying         lie → lying

NEGATIVE — add not after am/is/are
   I am not cooking.   She is not sleeping.

QUESTIONS — swap am/is/are to the front
   Are you cooking?    Is she sleeping?

PRESENT SIMPLE vs CONTINUOUS
   Simple = habit:       I eat rice every day.
   Continuous = now:     I am eating rice now.

TIME WORDS: now, right now, at the moment, today, listen!, look!

⚠️ Some verbs are NOT used in continuous form:
   like, love, know, want, need, understand
   ❌ I am knowing    ✅ I know
ruleZh: 现在进行时表示正在发生。用 am/is/are + 动词ing。否定在 be 后加 not。疑问把 be 放前面。习惯用简单时，正在做用进行时。like, know 等不用进行时。

title: Past Simple Tense
rule:
PAST SIMPLE — finished actions in the past.
   Yesterday I walked to the market.

REGULAR verbs: add -ed
   walk → walked      cook → cooked      clean → cleaned
   Ends in -e: add -d          like → liked
   Consonant + y: y → -ied     study → studied
   Short vowel + consonant: double it   stop → stopped

IRREGULAR verbs — memorise (no -ed)
   go → went        eat → ate         drink → drank
   see → saw        come → came       give → gave
   take → took      make → made       say → said
   have → had       do → did          run → ran
   buy → bought     bring → brought   think → thought
   get → got        find → found      tell → told
   sleep → slept    feel → felt       leave → left
   is/am → was      are → were

NEGATIVE — did not + PLAIN verb
   I did not go.      ⚠️ NOT 'did not went'

QUESTIONS — Did + PLAIN verb
   Did you go?        ⚠️ NOT 'Did you went?'

TIME WORDS: yesterday, last night, last week, in 2020, ago
ruleZh: 过去时表示已完成的事。规则动词加 -ed，不规则要背（go→went）。否定用 did not + 原形。疑问用 Did + 原形。用了 did 动词回到原形。

title: Past Continuous
rule:
PAST CONTINUOUS — happening at a moment in the past.
   I was cooking when you called.

FORM:  was / were  +  verb + ing
   I/He/She/It  was  cooking
   We/You/They  were cooking

MAIN USE — an action interrupted by another
   I WAS COOKING when the phone RANG.
   (long action = past continuous, short action = past simple)

ALSO — two actions at the same time
   She was cooking while I was cleaning.

ALSO — setting a scene
   It was raining and the wind was blowing.

NEGATIVE
   I was not cooking.   They were not sleeping.

QUESTIONS
   Were you cooking?    Was she sleeping?

PAST SIMPLE vs PAST CONTINUOUS
   Simple = completed:     I cooked dinner. (finished)
   Continuous = in progress: I was cooking dinner. (middle of it)
ruleZh: 过去进行时表示过去某刻正在做。用 was/were + 动词ing。常用于被打断的动作：I was cooking when you called。长动作用进行时，短动作用简单时。

title: Future Tense (will / going to)
rule:
TWO MAIN WAYS to talk about the future.

1. WILL  —  decisions now, promises, predictions
   I WILL help you.        (deciding right now)
   It WILL rain tomorrow.  (prediction)
   I WILL always love you. (promise)
   FORM: will + PLAIN verb (same for everyone)
   ⚠️ NOT 'will to help', NOT 'will helps'

   Negative: will not (won't)
      I will not go.  /  I won't go.
   Question: Will you help me?

2. GOING TO  —  plans already decided
   I AM GOING TO visit my sister. (already planned)
   FORM: am/is/are + going to + PLAIN verb
   Negative: I am not going to go.
   Question: Are you going to go?

3. PRESENT CONTINUOUS for fixed arrangements
   I am meeting the doctor at 3pm tomorrow.

WILL vs GOING TO
   Decide now:      The bag is heavy — I WILL help you.
   Already planned:  I AM GOING TO buy a new bag tomorrow.

TIME WORDS: tomorrow, next week, next year, soon, later, tonight
ruleZh: 将来时有两种：will 表示现在决定、承诺、预测，用 will + 原形。going to 表示已经计划好的事，用 am/is/are going to + 原形。否定 will not (won't)。

title: Present Perfect (have / has)
rule:
PRESENT PERFECT — the past connected to now.
   I HAVE eaten already.   She HAS finished her work.

FORM:  have / has  +  PAST PARTICIPLE
   I/You/We/They  have  eaten
   He/She/It      has   eaten

PAST PARTICIPLES
   Regular: same as past simple (add -ed)
      walked, cooked, cleaned, studied
   Irregular: often a third form
      go → went → GONE        eat → ate → EATEN
      see → saw → SEEN        do → did → DONE
      take → took → TAKEN     give → gave → GIVEN
      write → wrote → WRITTEN be → was → BEEN
      have → had → HAD        make → made → MADE

WHEN TO USE IT
   1. Finished, but time not stated
      I have eaten.  (we don't say when)
   2. Life experience
      I have been to Malaysia.
   3. Started in the past, still true
      I have lived here for ten years.
   4. Just finished
      She has just arrived.

PRESENT PERFECT vs PAST SIMPLE
   ✅ I have eaten.            (no time given)
   ✅ I ate at 7pm.            (specific time given)
   ❌ I have eaten yesterday.  (never with a past time!)

WORDS OFTEN USED: already, just, yet, ever, never, for, since
ruleZh: 现在完成时连接过去和现在，用 have/has + 过去分词。表示做完了但不说时间、人生经历、从过去持续到现在。有具体过去时间时用过去简单时，不能说 I have eaten yesterday。

title: Irregular Verbs (3 forms)
rule:
MOST VERBS ARE REGULAR — just add -ed
   walk → walked → walked
   cook → cooked → cooked

IRREGULAR VERBS have THREE different forms you must memorise:
   BASE  →  PAST  →  PAST PARTICIPLE

WHEN YOU NEED EACH FORM
   Base:            I EAT rice.  /  Did you EAT?
   Past:            I ATE rice yesterday.
   Past participle: I have EATEN.  /  It was EATEN.

THE MOST IMPORTANT ONES

   be      →  was/were  →  been
   have    →  had       →  had
   do      →  did       →  done
   go      →  went      →  gone
   eat     →  ate       →  eaten
   drink   →  drank     →  drunk
   see     →  saw       →  seen
   come    →  came      →  come
   give    →  gave      →  given
   take    →  took      →  taken
   make    →  made      →  made
   say     →  said      →  said
   get     →  got       →  got
   buy     →  bought    →  bought
   bring   →  brought   →  brought
   think   →  thought   →  thought
   teach   →  taught    →  taught
   find    →  found     →  found
   tell    →  told      →  told
   sleep   →  slept     →  slept
   feel    →  felt      →  felt
   leave   →  left      →  left
   write   →  wrote     →  written
   speak   →  spoke     →  spoken
   break   →  broke     →  broken
   run     →  ran       →  run
   sit     →  sat       →  sat
   read    →  read      →  read  (spelling same, sound changes!)
   put     →  put       →  put
   cut     →  cut       →  cut
ruleZh: 不规则动词有三个形式：原形、过去式、过去分词。原形用于现在时和 did 之后；过去式用于过去时；过去分词用于完成时和被动语态。要背：go-went-gone, eat-ate-eaten。

title: Using 'to' + verb (Infinitives)
rule:
INFINITIVE = to + PLAIN verb
   to eat,  to go,  to learn,  to help

USE 1 — after certain verbs
   want, need, like, love, hope, decide, try, plan, learn, forget, promise
      I WANT TO learn English.
      She DECIDED TO go home.
      I NEED TO buy rice.

USE 2 — to show purpose (why)
   I go to the market TO BUY vegetables.
   She studies TO PASS the exam.

USE 3 — after adjectives
   It is nice TO MEET you.
   I am happy TO help.
   English is easy TO learn.

⚠️ VERBS THAT TAKE -ING instead (not 'to')
   enjoy, finish, stop, avoid, mind, keep, practise
      ✅ I enjoy cooking.     ❌ I enjoy to cook.
      ✅ She finished eating. ❌ She finished to eat.

⚠️ AFTER MODALS — no 'to'
   ✅ I can swim.       ❌ I can to swim.
   ✅ She must go.      ❌ She must to go.

⚠️ NEVER change the verb after 'to'
   ✅ I want to eat.    ❌ I want to eats / to eating
ruleZh: 不定式是 to + 动词原形。用在 want, need, like, hope, decide 之后，也用来表示目的。但 enjoy, finish, stop 之后要用 -ing。情态动词后不加 to。to 后面动词永远用原形。

title: Modal Verbs (can, should, must)
rule:
MODAL VERBS add meaning to another verb.
   FORM: modal + PLAIN verb (never add -s, never add 'to')

CAN / CANNOT — ability or permission
   I CAN cook.        She CAN speak English.
   CAN I sit here?    (asking permission)

COULD — past ability, or polite request
   I COULD swim when I was young.
   COULD you help me please?  (very polite)

SHOULD / SHOULD NOT — advice
   You SHOULD rest.       You SHOULDN'T smoke.

MUST / MUST NOT — strong necessity or a rule
   I MUST go now.         You MUST NOT park here.

HAVE TO — necessity from outside (a rule)
   I HAVE TO work tomorrow.
   ⚠️ 'have to' DOES take 'to'. Modals do not.

MAY / MIGHT — possibility, or formal permission
   It MAY rain later.     It MIGHT be cold.
   MAY I come in?  (formal)

WOULD — polite offers, imagined situations
   WOULD you like tea?    I WOULD go if I had time.

⚠️ GOLDEN RULES
   ✅ She can swim.     ❌ She cans swim.  ❌ She can to swim.
   Negative: just add not → cannot, should not, must not
ruleZh: 情态动词后面用动词原形，不加 -s 也不加 to。can 能力，should 建议，must 必须，may/might 可能，would 礼貌。注意 have to 要加 to，情态动词不加。

title: Prepositions
rule:
PREPOSITIONS show place, time or direction.

PLACE
   in           inside:        in the bag, in Singapore
   on           on a surface:  on the table, on the wall
   under        below:         under the chair
   next to      at the side
   behind       at the back
   in front of  at the front
   between      in the middle of TWO
   among        in the middle of MANY
   opposite     facing

TIME
   at  exact times:        at 7 o'clock, at noon, at night
   on  days and dates:     on Monday, on 5 May
   in  months, years, long periods: in May, in 2026, in the morning

⚠️ at night  (not 'in the night')
⚠️ in the morning / afternoon / evening  BUT  at night

MOVEMENT
   to     towards:     I go to the market.
   from   starting:    I came from home.
   into   entering:    She walked into the room.
   out of leaving:     He came out of the shop.

COMMON MISTAKES
   ❌ I go to home      ✅ I go home
   ❌ in Monday         ✅ on Monday
   ❌ on the morning    ✅ in the morning
   ❌ arrive to         ✅ arrive at / arrive in
ruleZh: 介词表示地点、时间、方向。in 里面，on 表面，under 下面。时间：at 钟点，on 日期星期，in 月份年份。注意 at night。go home 不加 to。

title: Conjunctions (and, but, because)
rule:
CONJUNCTIONS join words, phrases or sentences.

BASIC JOINERS
   and      adds:        I cook AND she cleans.
   but      contrasts:   I am tired BUT happy.
   or       choices:     Tea OR coffee?
   so       result:      I was tired SO I slept.
   because  reason:      I am happy BECAUSE she came.

TIME JOINERS
   when     I cook WHEN she arrives.
   while    She cooked WHILE I cleaned.
   before   Wash your hands BEFORE you eat.
   after    We rest AFTER we work.
   until    Wait UNTIL I come back.
   as soon as Call me AS SOON AS you arrive.

CONTRAST JOINERS
   although / though   ALTHOUGH it rained, we went out.
   even though         EVEN THOUGH I was tired, I worked.
   however (formal)    It rained. HOWEVER, we went out.

⚠️ BECAUSE vs SO — opposite directions
   I stayed home BECAUSE it rained.  (reason comes after)
   It rained SO I stayed home.       (result comes after)

⚠️ Don't use both 'although' and 'but' together
   ❌ Although I was tired, but I worked.
   ✅ Although I was tired, I worked.
ruleZh: 连词连接句子。and 增加，but 转折，or 选择，so 结果，because 原因。时间用 when, while, before, after, until。转折用 although。不要 although 和 but 同时用。

title: Sentence Structure
rule:
Every English sentence needs a SUBJECT and a VERB.

BASIC ORDER:  SUBJECT + VERB + OBJECT
   Mama cooks dinner.
   I eat rice.
   She loves her family.

⚠️ English word order is FIXED. You cannot move parts freely.
   ✅ I eat rice every day.
   ❌ Every day rice I eat.

WHERE EXTRA INFORMATION GOES
   Subject + Verb + Object + Place + Time
   I ate rice at home yesterday.

TYPES OF SENTENCE
   Statement:  She is kind.
   Question:   Is she kind?
   Command:    Please sit down.
   Exclamation: What a lovely day!

SIMPLE / COMPOUND / COMPLEX
   Simple:   I cook rice.
   Compound: I cook rice AND she washes plates.  (two equal parts)
   Complex:  I cook rice BECAUSE we are hungry.  (one part depends)

FRAGMENTS — not real sentences (missing subject or verb)
   ❌ Going to the market.       ✅ I am going to the market.
   ❌ Because I was tired.       ✅ I slept because I was tired.

RUN-ON SENTENCES — need joining properly
   ❌ I was tired I slept.
   ✅ I was tired, so I slept.
ruleZh: 英语句子必须有主语和动词，顺序固定：主语+动词+宾语+地点+时间。简单句一个主谓，并列句用 and 连接，复合句用 because 等。片段句缺主语或动词，不算完整句子。

title: Asking Questions
rule:
TWO MAIN KINDS of question.

1. YES / NO QUESTIONS
   With BE — move be to the front
      She is tired.  →  IS she tired?
      They were here. →  WERE they here?
   With other verbs — use DO / DOES / DID
      You eat rice.  →  DO you eat rice?
      She eats rice. →  DOES she eat rice?
      You ate rice.  →  DID you eat rice?
   ⚠️ After do/does/did the verb stays PLAIN
      ❌ Does she eats?   ✅ Does she eat?
   With modals — move the modal
      Can you help?   Should I go?

2. WH- QUESTIONS — ask for information
   What    thing:     WHAT is your name?
   Who     person:    WHO is that?
   Where   place:     WHERE do you live?
   When    time:      WHEN do you eat?
   Why     reason:    WHY are you sad?
   How     manner:    HOW do you cook this?
   Which   choice:    WHICH bag is yours?
   Whose   owner:     WHOSE bag is this?

HOW + adjective
   How MANY children? (countable)
   How MUCH money? (uncountable)
   How OLD are you?     How LONG is it?
   How OFTEN do you go? How FAR is it?

STRUCTURE:  WH- + do/does/did + subject + plain verb
   WHERE DO you live?    WHY DID she leave?
ruleZh: 疑问句两种：是非问句用 be 提前或 Do/Does/Did。特殊疑问句用 What, Who, Where, When, Why, How。用了 do/does/did 动词要用原形。How many 数可数，How much 数不可数。

title: Making Negatives
rule:
HOW TO MAKE A SENTENCE NEGATIVE.

WITH 'BE' — just add not
   I am tired.      → I am NOT tired.
   She is here.     → She is NOT here.  (isn't)
   They were late.  → They were NOT late.  (weren't)

WITH OTHER VERBS — use do / does / did + not
   Present:
      I eat fish.    → I DO NOT eat fish.  (don't)
      She eats fish. → She DOES NOT eat fish.  (doesn't)
      ⚠️ The verb loses its -s!  NOT 'does not eats'
   Past:
      I ate fish.    → I DID NOT eat fish.  (didn't)
      ⚠️ Back to plain verb!  NOT 'did not ate'

WITH MODALS — add not
   can → cannot / can't
   will → will not / won't
   should → should not / shouldn't
   must → must not / mustn't

WITH PRESENT PERFECT
   I have eaten. → I have NOT eaten.  (haven't)

SHORT FORMS
   am not (no short form for I)   is not → isn't
   are not → aren't               was not → wasn't
   were not → weren't             do not → don't
   does not → doesn't             did not → didn't
   have not → haven't             has not → hasn't

⚠️ ONE negative only
   ❌ I don't have no money.    ✅ I don't have any money.
ruleZh: 否定句：be 动词后加 not。其他动词用 do/does/did not + 原形。用了 does/did 动词不加 -s 也不用过去式。情态动词加 not。英语只能有一个否定词。

title: Subject-Verb Agreement
rule:
THE VERB MUST MATCH THE SUBJECT.

BASIC RULE
   Singular subject → singular verb:  The cat IS sleeping.
   Plural subject   → plural verb:    The cats ARE sleeping.

PRESENT SIMPLE
   He/She/It → verb + s:   She walks.
   I/You/We/They → plain:  They walk.

TRICKY CASES

1. Words between subject and verb — ignore them!
   The bag of apples IS heavy.  (bag is the subject, not apples)
   The box of books IS on the table.

2. 'and' makes it plural
   Mama and Lin ARE here.

3. 'or' / 'either...or' — match the NEAREST one
   Either the cat or the dogs ARE hungry.
   Either the dogs or the cat IS hungry.

4. Collective nouns → usually singular
   My family IS large.   The team IS winning.

5. Uncountable nouns → always singular
   The water IS cold.    Rice IS cheap.

6. 'Everyone / everybody / someone / nobody' → SINGULAR
   Everyone IS here.  (not 'are')

7. Amounts of time or money → singular
   Ten dollars IS a lot.   Two hours IS enough.

8. 'There is' / 'There are'
   There IS one cat.   There ARE two cats.
ruleZh: 动词必须和主语一致。单数主语配单数动词。主语和动词之间的词要忽略：The bag of apples is heavy。and 连接是复数。everyone 是单数。集体名词通常单数。

title: Punctuation & Capital Letters
rule:
FULL STOP  .
   Ends a statement:  She is kind.
   Also for abbreviations: Mr. Dr. etc.

QUESTION MARK  ?
   Ends a question:  Are you tired?

EXCLAMATION MARK  !
   Strong feeling:  What a lovely day!  Be careful!
   Use sparingly — one is enough.

COMMA  ,
   Lists:              I bought rice, fish and eggs.
   After an opener:    Yesterday, I went out.
   Before but/so/and joining two sentences:
                       I was tired, so I slept.
   Around extra info:  Mama, my mother, is kind.
   ⚠️ Never join two sentences with only a comma
      ❌ I was tired, I slept.
      ✅ I was tired, so I slept.

APOSTROPHE  '
   Ownership:     Mama's bag
   Short forms:   don't, it's, can't

QUOTATION MARKS  " "
   Speech:  She said, "I am tired."
   Note: comma before, capital inside, full stop inside.

CAPITAL LETTERS — always for
   Start of a sentence:  She is kind.
   The word I:           I am here.
   Names:                Lin, Mr Tan
   Places:               Singapore, Bedok
   Days and months:      Monday, January
   Languages:            English, Chinese
   Titles of books/films

NOT capitalised: seasons (summer), subjects (maths), directions (north)
ruleZh: 句号结束陈述句，问号结束疑问句，感叹号表示强烈感情。逗号用于列举、开头状语、连接句子前。不能只用逗号连接两个句子。句首、I、人名、地名、星期月份、语言都要大写。

title: There is / There are
rule:
'THERE IS' and 'THERE ARE' say that something exists.

THERE IS  +  singular or uncountable
   There IS a cat in the garden.
   There IS some water in the cup.
   There IS a lot of rice.

THERE ARE  +  plural
   There ARE two cats in the garden.
   There ARE many people here.

PAST
   There WAS a cat.      (singular)
   There WERE two cats.  (plural)

NEGATIVE
   There is NOT any milk.  /  There isn't any milk.
   There are NO cats.      /  There aren't any cats.

QUESTIONS
   IS there a market nearby?
   ARE there any shops?
   HOW MANY cats are there?
   HOW MUCH milk is there?

⚠️ WITH A LIST — match the FIRST item
   There IS a cat and two dogs.
   There ARE two dogs and a cat.

⚠️ THERE vs THEIR vs THEY'RE
   there   = a place or 'there is'   →  There is a cat. / Sit there.
   their   = belonging to them       →  Their house is big.
   they're = they are                →  They're my friends.

⚠️ Don't confuse with HAVE
   ✅ There is a cat in my house.
   ✅ I have a cat.
ruleZh: There is 用于单数和不可数，There are 用于复数。过去时用 There was / There were。注意区分 there（那里）、their（他们的）、they're（他们是）。

title: Much, Many, Some, Any
rule:
WORDS THAT SHOW HOW MUCH OR HOW MANY.

MANY  +  countable plural
   many books, many people, many cats
   How MANY children?

MUCH  +  uncountable
   much water, much money, much time
   How MUCH money?

A LOT OF / LOTS OF  —  works with BOTH
   a lot of books ✅    a lot of water ✅
   Best for positive sentences.

SOME  —  positive sentences, both types
   I have SOME books.    I need SOME water.
   Also in offers: Would you like SOME tea?

ANY  —  negatives and questions
   I don't have ANY money.
   Do you have ANY questions?

A FEW / FEW  +  countable
   A FEW books = a small number (positive feeling)
   FEW books  = almost none (negative feeling)

A LITTLE / LITTLE  +  uncountable
   A LITTLE water = a small amount (positive)
   LITTLE water  = almost none (negative)

NO / NONE
   I have NO money.    How many are left? NONE.

⚠️ QUICK CHECK
   Can you count it?  →  many, a few, few
   Cannot count it?   →  much, a little, little
ruleZh: many 用于可数复数，much 用于不可数。a lot of 两者都行。some 用于肯定句，any 用于否定和疑问。a few 可数，a little 不可数。few/little 表示几乎没有。

title: Numbers, Time & Dates
rule:
SAYING NUMBERS

   13 thirteen  vs  30 thirty     ⚠️ Listen for the ending!
   14 fourteen  vs  40 forty
   15 fifteen   vs  50 fifty
   The -TEEN numbers stress the END: thirTEEN
   The -TY numbers stress the START: THIRty

   100  a hundred / one hundred
   1,000  a thousand
   250  two hundred AND fifty  (British English uses 'and')

TELLING THE TIME
   7:00   seven o'clock
   7:15   quarter past seven  /  seven fifteen
   7:30   half past seven     /  seven thirty
   7:45   quarter to eight    /  seven forty-five
   7:05   five past seven
   7:50   ten to eight
   12:00 noon = midday        12:00 night = midnight

   am = morning (before 12)      pm = afternoon/evening

DATES
   Written: 5 May 2026  or  5/5/2026
   Said: "the fifth of May" or "May the fifth"
   ⚠️ Use ORDINAL numbers for dates:
      1st first, 2nd second, 3rd third, 4th fourth,
      5th fifth, 12th twelfth, 20th twentieth, 21st twenty-first

MONEY
   $5.50 → five dollars fifty  /  five fifty
   "How much is it?"  "It costs twelve dollars."

AGE
   I am forty.  /  I am forty years old.
   ⚠️ NOT 'I have forty years'

PHONE NUMBERS — say each digit separately
   9123 4567 → nine one two three, four five six seven
   0 is said as "oh" or "zero"

title: Prefixes & Suffixes
rule:
A PREFIX goes at the START and changes meaning.
A SUFFIX goes at the END and often changes the word type.

PREFIXES THAT MEAN 'NOT'
   un-   unhappy, unkind, unfair, unable, unusual
   in-   incorrect, impossible (im- before m/p), invisible
   dis-  dislike, disagree, dishonest, disappear
   non-  non-stop, nonsense

OTHER USEFUL PREFIXES
   re-    again:        redo, rewrite, return, replay
   pre-   before:       preschool, prepare, preview
   over-  too much:     overeat, overwork, oversleep
   under- too little:   underpaid, underweight
   mis-   wrongly:      misunderstand, mistake, misspell

SUFFIXES THAT MAKE NOUNS
   -er / -or   person who does it:  teacher, driver, actor, visitor
   -ness       state of being:      kindness, happiness, darkness
   -tion       action or result:    action, education, information
   -ment       result:              payment, movement, government
   -ity        quality:             ability, activity, safety

SUFFIXES THAT MAKE ADJECTIVES
   -ful    full of:      helpful, careful, beautiful, useful
   -less   without:      helpless, careless, useless, homeless
   -able   can be done:  comfortable, washable, readable
   -y      like:         rainy, sunny, healthy, dirty

SUFFIX THAT MAKES ADVERBS
   -ly     quickly, slowly, carefully, happily

💡 THE POWER OF THIS
   Learn 'care' and you get:
   careful, careless, carefully, carelessly, caring, uncaring
ruleZh: 前缀放在词首改变意思：un-, in-, dis-, non- 表示「不」；re- 表示「再」；over- 太多；mis- 错误。后缀放在词尾改变词性：-er 人，-ness 状态，-ful 充满，-less 没有，-ly 副词。

title: Word Families
rule:
ONE WORD CAN BECOME MANY WORDS.
Learn the family and your vocabulary multiplies.

   VERB → NOUN (person) → NOUN (thing) → ADJECTIVE → ADVERB

EXAMPLES

   teach  → teacher  → teaching  → —          → —
   act    → actor    → action    → active     → actively
   help   → helper   → help      → helpful    → helpfully
   care   → carer    → care      → careful    → carefully
   beauty → —        → beauty    → beautiful  → beautifully
   decide → decider  → decision  → decisive   → decisively
   succeed→ —        → success   → successful → successfully
   create → creator  → creation  → creative   → creatively
   inform → informer → information→ informative→ —
   happy  → —        → happiness → happy      → happily
   safe   → —        → safety    → safe       → safely
   differ → —        → difference→ different  → differently
   friend → friend   → friendship→ friendly   → —

HOW TO KNOW WHICH FORM TO USE
   Before a NOUN → adjective:      a HELPFUL person
   After BE      → adjective:      She is HELPFUL.
   Describing a VERB → adverb:     She helped CAREFULLY.
   The thing itself → noun:        Thank you for your HELP.
   The doer → -er/-or noun:        She is a HELPER.

💡 TEST YOURSELF
   Cover one column and try to say the others.
ruleZh: 一个词可以变成很多词。teach → teacher → teaching。名词前用形容词，be 后用形容词，修饰动词用副词，做人用 -er。学会一个词族等于学会好几个词。

title: Spelling Rules & Patterns
rule:
SILENT LETTERS — written but not said
   silent K:  know, knife, knee, knock
   silent W:  write, wrong, two, answer
   silent B:  lamb, comb, climb, thumb
   silent H:  hour, honest
   silent GH: night, light, through
   silent L:  half, walk, talk, could

'I BEFORE E' RULE
   i before e:              believe, friend, piece, field
   EXCEPT after c:          receive, ceiling
   or when it sounds 'ay':  eight, neighbour, weight

ADDING -ED or -ING
   Drop the -e:             make → making, hope → hoped
   Double the consonant (short vowel + 1 consonant):
                            stop → stopped, run → running
   Consonant + y → -ied:    study → studied, cry → cried
   Vowel + y → just add:    play → played, enjoy → enjoyed

DOUBLE LETTERS to watch
   necessary, address, success, occasion, committee,
   embarrass, tomorrow (one m!), until (one l!)

WORDS OFTEN MISSPELLED
   ✅ because       ❌ becuase
   ✅ friend        ❌ freind
   ✅ beautiful     ❌ beutiful
   ✅ definitely    ❌ definately
   ✅ separate      ❌ seperate
   ✅ received      ❌ recieved
   ✅ which         ❌ wich
   ✅ tomorrow      ❌ tommorow

PLURAL SPELLING → see the Nouns topic
ruleZh: 注意不发音字母：know 的 k，write 的 w，hour 的 h。i 在 e 前面（believe），但 c 后面相反（receive）。加 -ed/-ing：去 e（make→making），双写辅音（stop→stopped），辅音+y 改 -ied。

title: Verb + Preposition Patterns
rule:
SOME VERBS ALWAYS TAKE A PARTICULAR PREPOSITION.
These must be memorised — there is no rule.

VERB + TO
   listen TO music        belong TO me         talk TO her
   happen TO him          reply TO the email   look forward TO

VERB + FOR
   wait FOR the bus       look FOR my keys     pay FOR the food
   ask FOR help           thank you FOR ...    apply FOR a job

VERB + ON
   depend ON you          rely ON her          concentrate ON work
   spend money ON food    congratulate ON

VERB + ABOUT
   talk ABOUT it          think ABOUT it       worry ABOUT money
   complain ABOUT noise   dream ABOUT

VERB + WITH
   agree WITH you         help WITH homework   argue WITH him
   deal WITH a problem

VERB + AT
   look AT the picture    laugh AT the joke    shout AT someone
   arrive AT a place (small) / arrive IN a country

VERB + OF
   think OF an idea       remind me OF her     consist OF
   take care OF

ADJECTIVE + PREPOSITION
   good AT English        bad AT maths        interested IN art
   afraid OF spiders      proud OF you        tired OF waiting
   worried ABOUT money    married TO him      famous FOR food

⚠️ NO PREPOSITION NEEDED
   ❌ discuss about it   ✅ discuss it
   ❌ enter into a room  ✅ enter a room
   ❌ answer to the question  ✅ answer the question
   ❌ marry with him     ✅ marry him

title: Comparing Things
rule:
COMPARING TWO THINGS — comparative
   Add -er + than (short words)
      big → bigger than,  tall → taller than
   Ends in -e: add -r
      nice → nicer than
   Short vowel + consonant: double it
      big → bigger,  hot → hotter,  thin → thinner
   Ends in -y: y → -ier
      happy → happier,  busy → busier
   Long words (2+ syllables): more ... than
      more beautiful than,  more expensive than

COMPARING THREE OR MORE — superlative
   Short: the + -est        the biggest, the tallest
   -y words: the + -iest    the happiest
   Long: the most           the most beautiful

IRREGULAR (memorise)
   good → better → the best
   bad → worse → the worst
   far → further → the furthest
   many → more → the most
   little → less → the least

EQUAL COMPARISON — as ... as
   She is AS tall AS me.
   It is NOT AS hot AS yesterday.

⚠️ NEVER DOUBLE UP
   ❌ more bigger        ✅ bigger
   ❌ most biggest       ✅ the biggest
   ❌ more better        ✅ better

⚠️ Always use THE with superlatives
   ✅ She is the best.   ❌ She is best.
ruleZh: 比较两个用 -er + than 或 more...than。三个以上用 the -est 或 the most。不规则：good→better→best, bad→worse→worst。同等比较用 as...as。不能重复 more bigger。

title: Confusing Word Pairs
rule:
WORDS THAT SOUND ALIKE BUT MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS.

ITS vs IT'S
   its  = belonging to it     The dog wagged ITS tail.
   it's = it is / it has      IT'S raining.

THEIR / THERE / THEY'RE
   their   = belonging to them   THEIR house is big.
   there   = that place          Sit over THERE.
   they're = they are            THEY'RE my friends.

YOUR vs YOU'RE
   your   = belonging to you   Is this YOUR bag?
   you're = you are            YOU'RE very kind.

TO / TOO / TWO
   to  = direction or infinitive   I go TO work. I want TO eat.
   too = also, or excessive        Me TOO. It is TOO hot.
   two = the number 2              I have TWO cats.

THEN vs THAN
   then = next in time      First eat, THEN rest.
   than = comparing         Bigger THAN mine.

LOSE vs LOOSE
   lose  = to not find      Don't LOSE your keys.
   loose = not tight        My shirt is LOOSE.

AFFECT vs EFFECT
   affect = verb (to change)   Rain AFFECTS my mood.
   effect = noun (a result)    The EFFECT was clear.

ADVICE vs ADVISE
   advice = noun    She gave me good ADVICE.
   advise = verb    I ADVISE you to rest.

QUIET vs QUITE
   quiet = not noisy    Please be QUIET.
   quite = fairly       It is QUITE hot.
ruleZh: 易混淆词：its 所属 / it's 是 it is。their 他们的 / there 那里 / they're 他们是。your 你的 / you're 你是。to 到 / too 也太 / two 二。then 然后 / than 比。

title: Passive Voice
rule:
ACTIVE — the subject does the action
   Mama COOKED the rice.
   (Mama = doer, rice = receiver)

PASSIVE — the subject receives the action
   The rice WAS COOKED by Mama.
   (rice = receiver, now the subject)

FORM:  be  +  PAST PARTICIPLE
   Present: The rice IS cooked.
   Past:    The rice WAS cooked.
   Future:  The rice WILL BE cooked.
   Perfect: The rice HAS BEEN cooked.

HOW TO CHANGE ACTIVE → PASSIVE
   1. Move the object to the front
   2. Add the correct form of 'be'
   3. Change the verb to a past participle
   4. Add 'by + doer' only if needed

   Active:  She wrote the letter.
   Passive: The letter WAS WRITTEN by her.

WHEN TO USE PASSIVE
   The doer is unknown:     My bag WAS STOLEN.
   The doer is unimportant: The road WAS REPAIRED.
   Formal or official:      Applications MUST BE SUBMITTED by Friday.
   Rules and notices:       Shoes MUST BE REMOVED.

⚠️ You need the PAST PARTICIPLE, not the past simple
   ❌ The rice was cook.     ✅ The rice was cooked.
   ❌ The letter was wrote.  ✅ The letter was written.
ruleZh: 主动语态主语做动作，被动语态主语受动作。被动用 be + 过去分词：The rice was cooked。不知道或不重要谁做时用被动。要用过去分词不是过去式。

title: Reported Speech
rule:
DIRECT SPEECH — the exact words in quotation marks
   She said, "I am tired."

REPORTED SPEECH — telling what someone said, no quotes
   She said (that) she WAS tired.

WHAT CHANGES

1. TENSE goes back one step
   am/is  → was          are → were
   eat    → ate          will → would
   can    → could        have → had
   ate    → had eaten

2. PRONOUNS change to match the speaker
   "I am tired" → She said SHE was tired.
   "My bag"     → She said HER bag.

3. TIME AND PLACE WORDS change
   now      → then
   today    → that day
   tomorrow → the next day
   yesterday → the day before
   here     → there
   this     → that

EXAMPLES
   "I am busy."          → He said he WAS busy.
   "I will come."        → He said he WOULD come.
   "I can help."         → He said he COULD help.
   "I ate lunch."        → He said he HAD EATEN lunch.

REPORTED QUESTIONS — no question mark, normal word order
   "Where do you live?" → She asked where I LIVED.
   "Are you tired?"     → She asked IF I WAS tired.

REPORTED COMMANDS — use 'to'
   "Sit down."      → She told me TO SIT down.
   "Don't be late." → She told me NOT TO BE late.
ruleZh: 间接引语转述别人的话，时态往前退一步：am→was, will→would, can→could。代词和时间词也要变。疑问句用 if 或 wh-词，语序正常。命令用 told me to。

title: If Sentences (Conditionals)
rule:
IF SENTENCES talk about a condition and its result.

ZERO CONDITIONAL — always true (facts)
   IF + present, ... present
   IF you heat water, it BOILS.
   IF it rains, the ground GETS wet.

FIRST CONDITIONAL — real future possibility
   IF + present, ... WILL + verb
   IF it rains, I WILL stay home.
   IF you study, you WILL pass.
   ⚠️ Never 'if it will rain' — the if-part stays present!

SECOND CONDITIONAL — imaginary now
   IF + past, ... WOULD + verb
   IF I HAD money, I WOULD travel.
   IF I WERE you, I WOULD rest.
   ⚠️ Use 'were' for all persons: If I were, if he were

THIRD CONDITIONAL — imaginary past (regret)
   IF + had + past participle, ... WOULD HAVE + past participle
   IF I HAD STUDIED, I WOULD HAVE PASSED.
   (but I didn't study, so I didn't pass)

QUICK GUIDE
   Fact:            If you heat ice, it melts.
   Likely future:   If it rains, I will stay home.
   Imaginary now:   If I had money, I would travel.
   Past regret:     If I had known, I would have come.

⚠️ THE COMMA
   If it rains, I will stay home.   (comma when 'if' is first)
   I will stay home if it rains.    (no comma when 'if' is second)
ruleZh: 条件句四种：零条件表示事实（if + 现在，现在）。第一条件表示可能的将来（if + 现在，will）。第二条件表示假想（if + 过去，would）。第三条件表示过去后悔（if had + 过去分词，would have）。

title: Relative Clauses (who, which, that)
rule:
RELATIVE CLAUSES add information about a noun.
   The woman WHO cooks is my mother.

WHICH WORD TO USE
   who     → people        The woman WHO cooks...
   which   → things        The bag WHICH is green...
   that    → people or things (informal, very common)
   whose   → ownership     The man WHOSE bag was stolen...
   where   → places        The market WHERE I shop...
   when    → times         The day WHEN we met...

HOW TO COMBINE TWO SENTENCES
   The woman is my mother. She cooks well.
   → The woman WHO cooks well is my mother.

   I bought a bag. It is green.
   → I bought a bag WHICH is green.

DEFINING clauses — essential information, no commas
   The man WHO called is my brother.
   (tells us which man)

NON-DEFINING clauses — extra information, use commas
   My brother, WHO lives in Malaysia, is a teacher.
   (we already know which brother)
   ⚠️ Never use 'that' in non-defining clauses.

⚠️ Don't repeat the subject
   ❌ The woman who she cooks is my mother.
   ✅ The woman who cooks is my mother.
ruleZh: 关系从句补充说明名词。who 指人，which 指物，that 两者都行，whose 表示所属，where 指地点。必要信息不加逗号，额外信息加逗号。不要重复主语。

title: Reading Comprehension Skills
rule:
HOW TO READ A PASSAGE PROPERLY

STEP 1 — Read the questions FIRST
   Now you know what to look for.

STEP 2 — Skim the whole passage quickly
   Get the general idea. Don't stop at hard words.

STEP 3 — Scan for the answer
   Find key words from the question in the passage.

STEP 4 — Read that part slowly and answer

FINDING THE MAIN IDEA
   Usually in the FIRST or LAST sentence of a paragraph.
   Ask: "What is this mostly about?"
   Not a small detail — the big picture.

TYPES OF QUESTION

   LITERAL — the answer is written in the passage
      "What time did she leave?" → find it and copy it
   INFERENCE — the answer is hinted, not stated
      "How did she feel?" → look for clues
      'She slammed the door' → she was angry
   VOCABULARY — what does a word mean here
      Read the whole sentence around it
   OWN WORDS — do not copy, rewrite it

GUESSING UNKNOWN WORDS
   1. Read the whole sentence
   2. Is it a person, thing, action or description?
   3. Look for clues before and after
   4. Look for a familiar part: 'unhelpful' → help
   5. Move on if it's not needed for the answer

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKES
   Answering from your own opinion instead of the passage
   Copying too much
   Not answering what was actually asked
   Leaving a question blank — always write something

title: Writing Messages & Letters
rule:
INFORMAL MESSAGE (to family or friends)
   Opening:  Hi Lin,  /  Dear Lin,
   Body:     Short and friendly.
   Closing:  See you soon!  /  Love, Mama  /  Take care!

   Example:
      Hi Lin,
      Hope you are well. I bought some fish at the market today.
      Come for dinner on Sunday?
      Love, Mama

FORMAL LETTER OR EMAIL (school, clinic, government)
   Opening:
      Dear Sir / Madam,        (you don't know the name)
      Dear Mr Tan,             (you know the name)
   First line — say WHY you are writing:
      I am writing to ask about...
      I am writing to inform you that...
      I would like to request...
   Body — clear and polite, one idea per paragraph
   Closing:
      Yours faithfully,   (if you used Dear Sir/Madam)
      Yours sincerely,    (if you used their name)
      Then your full name

   Example:
      Dear Sir / Madam,
      I am writing to request a change of appointment.
      My appointment is on 5 May at 3pm. Unfortunately I am
      unable to attend. Could it be moved to the following week?
      Thank you for your help.
      Yours faithfully,
      Mary Tan

USEFUL POLITE PHRASES
   I would like to...        Could you please...
   I am sorry to inform...   Thank you for your time.
   I look forward to hearing from you.

⚠️ FORMAL vs INFORMAL
   Formal:   I would like to request...  /  I am unable to attend.
   Informal: Can I change it?  /  I can't come.
   ❌ Never use short forms (can't, don't) in a formal letter.

title: Connecting Words for Writing
rule:
CONNECTING WORDS make your writing flow.

ORDER AND SEQUENCE
   Firstly, ...        First of all, ...
   Secondly, ...       Next, ...       Then, ...
   After that, ...     Finally, ...    Lastly, ...

ADDING MORE
   also                In addition, ...
   Furthermore, ...    Moreover, ...
   as well as          besides

GIVING EXAMPLES
   For example, ...    For instance, ...
   such as             like

SHOWING CONTRAST
   but                 However, ...
   On the other hand, ...
   Although / Even though ...
   In contrast, ...    Nevertheless, ...

SHOWING REASON
   because             since         as
   due to              because of

SHOWING RESULT
   so                  Therefore, ...
   As a result, ...    Consequently, ...
   Thus, ...

CONCLUDING
   In conclusion, ...  To conclude, ...
   Overall, ...        In summary, ...
   To sum up, ...

⚠️ PUNCTUATION
   Most of these formal ones take a comma:
      However, I disagree.
      Therefore, we should rest.
   But 'because' and 'so' do not:
      I rested because I was tired.

⚠️ DON'T START A SENTENCE WITH 'And' or 'But' in formal writing
   Use 'In addition' or 'However' instead.
